bull_bear.body: Prioritizing A&P spend (mid-teens % of revenue), HCP engagement, retail visibility, talent acquisition, and AI/digital tech. No dividends or buybacks mentioned; all capital directed toward growth levers.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Delayed OTC regulation; recall recurrence; execution risk in doubling HCP/reach; competition from local players; reliance on FMCH talent retention; potential channel conflict with indirect distributors.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly confident, energetic, and transformational. Management emphasizes empowerment, agility, challenger mindset, and India-first autonomy. Strong focus on culture, diversity, and accountability. Open to innovation and external models (e.g., 3rd party reps) if cost-effective.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Despite minimal past marketing, legacy brands (Avil, Combiflam) retain top market positions — indicating immense latent brand equity. B-Corp certification is rare in Indian FMCH and signals long-term ESG credibility. AI is already generating creatives in-house — a first for an Indian pharma subsidiary.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Portfolio of category-leading, decades-trusted OTC/self-care brands (Allegra, Combiflam, Avil, DePURA) with established consumer recall
- Strong distribution network spanning wholesalers, government institutions, modern pharmacy chains and e-commerce platforms
- Backed by Sanofi/Opella global consumer-healthcare heritage of scientific rigour, evidence-based formulations and quality standards
- Renewed, focused marketing and demand-generation investment behind legacy brands for the first time in over a decade, re-establishing consumer and HCP engagement
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Change in ultimate controlling shareholder — Following Sanofi's global sale of its consumer healthcare business, Opal Bidco SAS (majority voting control held by the Clayton, Dubilier & Rice Group) now exercises ultimate indirect control over the Company, and a mandatory open offer to public shareholders was triggered under SEBI SAST Regulations.
- Key managerial personnel turnover — The CFO role changed hands twice during the year: Ms. Maithilee Mistry (Whole-time Director & CFO) resigned effective 5th May 2025; Mr. Narahari Naidu was appointed CFO effective 4th August 2025 and resigned effective 15th October 2025; Mr. Richard D'souza was then appointed CFO effective 16th October 2025.
- Global trade and input-cost volatility — Geopolitical tensions (West Asia, Russia-Ukraine), evolving tariffs and trade regulations have raised procurement and freight costs and caused cargo delays and supply disruptions for businesses dependent on imported inputs and cross-border sourcing.
- Raw material cost volatility and regulatory scrutiny — The consumer healthcare industry faces raw material cost volatility, regulatory scrutiny and product standardisation requirements, which can pressure margins and compliance costs.
- Intensifying competitive landscape — Increasing participation by pharmaceutical companies, FMCG players and digital-first wellness brands is intensifying competition across product categories and distribution channels.
- Macroeconomic/consumption sensitivity — Business performance is linked to Indian consumer demand and disposable-income trends, which are influenced by inflation (CPI reaching 3.4% as of March 2026) and broader macroeconomic and global-trade conditions.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Allergy (Allegra #3 by value); Pain (Combiflam #5); Vitamin D (DePURA #5); VMS (emerging). All brands are market leaders in volume or value within their categories. No new segment launches yet, but category expansion under evaluation.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers (listed names)

business.body:
- "Case for separation: Play in Consumer Healthcare by its rules" — the deck contrasts a Pharma Approach (prescription driven, win with patented formulations, low single digit A&P) with a Consumer Healthcare Approach (win on brand equity, synergy of prescriptions and self choice, off-patent brands fund new launches, A&P investments mid teens).
- Leading brands as per IQVIA MAT Dec'25: Avil #1 by volume, Allegra #3 by value, Combiflam #5 by volume and DePura #5 (marked '# Pre Recall').
- Mission is "Health. In your hands. By making selfcare as simple as it should be" and vision is to "Become the best FMCH In & For India", executed through three pillars: Scale HCP Initiation, Scale Consumer Engagement and Improve Access.
- Deck characterises the starting point as "constrained demand generation" across Health Care Professionals, Consumer and Point of Sale, with the claim "We have unlocked demand levers after a long gap".
- Empowered country management is claimed via "Complete ownership of Global Brand P&L", an "India-first approach to innovations for Global brands too", while benefiting from "Opella's Global Scale, R&D & technology".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Demerger & listing] Timeline given as: 2021 investments curtailed and nutra business hived off; 2021-2022 manpower rationalization; Jun 2024 demerger into a separate entity; Jul 2024 voluntary recalls; Sep 2024 successful listing at the exchange; Dec 2024 new identity and workplace — the period is labelled "Turbulent start for an organization still taking shape".
- [Ownership change] "CD&R acquires controlling stake in CFC business globally. April '25" and "Sanofi CHC business renamed as Opella" — the deck refers to benefiting from Opella's global scale, R&D and technology.
- [Product recalls] Voluntary Recalls occurred in Jul 2024; the FY2025 brand-ranking slide carries the footnote "# Pre Recall" against DePura's #5 rank, so that rank is stated on a pre-recall basis.
- [Talent build] "Building FMCH talent with 60 new hires", alongside unlocking FMCH marketing and building FMCH GTM; culture described as a challenger mindset with speed, accountability and differentiated rewards.
- [Presented by] Deck was presented at the SCHIL Institutional Investor Meet on 24 March 2026 by Himanshu Bakshi, Managing Director.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Sanofi Consumer Healthcare India Limited (SCHIL) manufactures and sells pharmaceutical/consumer-healthcare (drugs and pharmaceuticals) products under a Fast-Moving Consumer Healthcare model that combines the scientific trust of healthcare with the speed and reach of consumer retail. It distributes through wholesalers, government institutions, modern pharmacy chains and e-commerce platforms across India, and in 2025 commenced export operations, adding an international dimension to its growth.

outlook.body: No forward-looking guidance provided; management emphasized growth and penetration as core focus with profitable trajectory.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Pipeline includes potential new launches from Opella global R&D (e.g., Allegra D as precedent); exploration of gastro/enterogermina/laxatives categories; crowdsourced innovation initiatives underway; potential product transfers from parent entity under board review.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Strengthen the core brand portfolio (Allegra, Combiflam, Avil, DePURA) through disciplined, focused marketing and demand-generation investment
- Expand access across channels and geographies, including scaling the nascent export business
- Accelerate digital and future-ready capabilities, including AI-enabled insights for faster, better-informed decisions
- Run a synergistic demand-generation model integrating Healthcare Professional (HCP) recommendation, consumer engagement and retail availability
- Simplify the organisation ('radically simple') by streamlining decision-making and processes to enhance agility
- Continue innovation agenda with science-backed product launches (e.g. Allegra-D) addressing targeted consumer needs
- Leverage the scale and innovation capabilities of parent Opella Healthcare to support growth
- The Board recommended a final dividend of Rs 75 per equity share (face value Rs 10) for the Financial Year ended 31st December 2025, placed for shareholder approval at the AGM; no other multi-year dividend/buyback/debt-reduction policy is stated in this bundle.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: No new plant, site or manufacturing-capacity expansion is disclosed; the Company reports no owned manufacturing plants (BRSR shows 0 plants nationally/internationally, only 1 national office), consistent with a toll-manufacturing/outsourced production model. The stated expansion during the year was commercial and geographic rather than industrial: the Company commenced export operations in 2025, adding an international dimension to its distribution footprint, and continued to expand its FMCH distribution network (wholesalers, government institutions, modern pharmacy chains and e-commerce) and invest in 'future-ready' digital systems.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Consumer behaviour is shifting from reactive treatment-led consumption towards preventive and lifestyle-oriented healthcare spending
- Large under-penetration in consumer healthcare categories in India (an estimated 70-80% of the population Vitamin D deficient, 30-40% with allergy-related conditions) with low awareness/treatment levels is seen as a growth opportunity
- Rising health awareness, increasing self-care adoption, improving disposable incomes and growth in nutraceuticals/dietary supplements support industry demand
- Digital platforms and e-commerce are expanding accessibility and product penetration into Tier II and Tier III markets
- Evolving OTC regulatory framework, pricing pressures and increasing competitive intensity (from pharma, FMCG and digital-first wellness brands) are expected to shape the sector
- Raw material cost volatility, regulatory scrutiny and product standardisation requirements remain industry headwinds
- Export portfolio is gaining momentum, expanding geographic footprint and diversifying the business beyond India

deepdive.thesis: Sanofi Consumer Healthcare India is transforming from a legacy pharma division into a high-growth FMCH leader by reinvesting in brand equity, consumer education, and digital-first demand generation, leveraging its top-tier portfolio and India-first autonomy to capture rising self-medication trends. Profitable growth is being driven by doubling HCP reach, expanding retail access, and AI-enabled marketing, with OTC regulation as a key near-term catalyst.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: SCHIL is a Fast-Moving Consumer Healthcare (FMCH) company in India built on legacy self-care brands (Allegra, Combiflam, Avil, DePURA), combining pharmaceutical-grade scientific trust with consumer-retail distribution reach.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Sanofi Consumer Healthcare India Limited (SCHIL) manufactures and sells pharmaceutical/consumer-healthcare (drugs and pharmaceuticals) products under a Fast-Moving Consumer Healthcare model that combines the scientific trust of healthcare with the speed and reach of consumer retail. It distributes through wholesalers, government institutions, modern pharmacy chains and e-commerce platforms across India, and in 2025 commenced export operations, adding an international dimension to its growth.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- Sanofi India Limited — related party: Group company under common control (Section 2(76), Companies Act); counterparty for purchase of goods, availing toll manufacturing and other support services, expense reimbursement, licence fees/lease charges for premises, and sale/purchase of raw material/packaging materials
- Opella Healthcare India Private Limited — related party: Group company under common control; counterparty for provision and receipt of services
- Opella Healthcare International SAS — related party: Group company under common control; counterparty for purchase and sale of goods

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Allergy (Allegra #3 by value); Pain (Combiflam #5); Vitamin D (DePURA #5); VMS (emerging). All brands are market leaders in volume or value within their categories. No new segment launches yet, but category expansion under evaluation.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Allergy Relief:** Allegra, Allegra M, Allegra D, Allegra Nasal, Allegra Nasal Duo, Allegra-D, Avil
- **Pain Care:** Combiflam
- **Physical Wellness:** DePURA Kids Drops, DePURA 60,000 IU

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- India (29 states)
- International exports to 4 countries (~19% of turnover)

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: No forward-looking guidance provided; management emphasized growth and penetration as core focus with profitable trajectory.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Pipeline includes potential new launches from Opella global R&D (e.g., Allegra D as precedent); exploration of gastro/enterogermina/laxatives categories; crowdsourced innovation initiatives underway; potential product transfers from parent entity under board review.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Consumer behaviour is shifting from reactive treatment-led consumption towards preventive and lifestyle-oriented healthcare spending
- Large under-penetration in consumer healthcare categories in India (an estimated 70-80% of the population Vitamin D deficient, 30-40% with allergy-related conditions) with low awareness/treatment levels is seen as a growth opportunity
- Rising health awareness, increasing self-care adoption, improving disposable incomes and growth in nutraceuticals/dietary supplements support industry demand
- Digital platforms and e-commerce are expanding accessibility and product penetration into Tier II and Tier III markets
- Evolving OTC regulatory framework, pricing pressures and increasing competitive intensity (from pharma, FMCG and digital-first wellness brands) are expected to shape the sector
- Raw material cost volatility, regulatory scrutiny and product standardisation requirements remain industry headwinds
- Export portfolio is gaining momentum, expanding geographic footprint and diversifying the business beyond India

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Operating margin at 37%; ANP investment increased from low single-digit to mid-teens; supply chain fully localized in India, reducing dependency on global inputs and improving cost control.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Prioritizing A&P spend (mid-teens % of revenue), HCP engagement, retail visibility, talent acquisition, and AI/digital tech. No dividends or buybacks mentioned; all capital directed toward growth levers.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: No new plant, site or manufacturing-capacity expansion is disclosed; the Company reports no owned manufacturing plants (BRSR shows 0 plants nationally/internationally, only 1 national office), consistent with a toll-manufacturing/outsourced production model. The stated expansion during the year was commercial and geographic rather than industrial: the Company commenced export operations in 2025, adding an international dimension to its distribution footprint, and continued to expand its FMCH distribution network (wholesalers, government institutions, modern pharmacy chains and e-commerce) and invest in 'future-ready' digital systems.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Highly confident, energetic, and transformational. Management emphasizes empowerment, agility, challenger mindset, and India-first autonomy. Strong focus on culture, diversity, and accountability. Open to innovation and external models (e.g., 3rd party reps) if cost-effective.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Portfolio of category-leading, decades-trusted OTC/self-care brands (Allegra, Combiflam, Avil, DePURA) with established consumer recall
- Strong distribution network spanning wholesalers, government institutions, modern pharmacy chains and e-commerce platforms
- Backed by Sanofi/Opella global consumer-healthcare heritage of scientific rigour, evidence-based formulations and quality standards
- Renewed, focused marketing and demand-generation investment behind legacy brands for the first time in over a decade, re-establishing consumer and HCP engagement

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Delayed OTC regulation; recall recurrence; execution risk in doubling HCP/reach; competition from local players; reliance on FMCH talent retention; potential channel conflict with indirect distributors.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Despite minimal past marketing, legacy brands (Avil, Combiflam) retain top market positions — indicating immense latent brand equity. B-Corp certification is rare in Indian FMCH and signals long-term ESG credibility. AI is already generating creatives in-house — a first for an Indian pharma subsidiary.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Strengthen the core brand portfolio (Allegra, Combiflam, Avil, DePURA) through disciplined, focused marketing and demand-generation investment
- Expand access across channels and geographies, including scaling the nascent export business
- Accelerate digital and future-ready capabilities, including AI-enabled insights for faster, better-informed decisions
- Run a synergistic demand-generation model integrating Healthcare Professional (HCP) recommendation, consumer engagement and retail availability
- Simplify the organisation ('radically simple') by streamlining decision-making and processes to …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Demerger & listing] Timeline given as: 2021 investments curtailed and nutra business hived off; 2021-2022 manpower rationalization; Jun 2024 demerger into a separate entity; Jul 2024 voluntary recalls; Sep 2024 successful listing at the exchange; Dec 2024 new identity and workplace — the period is labelled "Turbulent start for an organization still taking shape".
- [Ownership change] "CD&R acquires controlling stake in CFC business globally. April '25" and "Sanofi CHC business renamed as Opella" — the deck refers to benefiting from Opella's global scale, R&D and technology.
- [Product recalls] Voluntary Recalls occurred in Jul 2024; the FY2025 brand-ranking slide carries the footnote "# Pre Recall" against DePura's #5 rank, so that rank is stated on a pre-recall basis.
- [Talent build] "Building FMCH talent with 60 new hires", alongside unlocking FMCH marketing and building FMCH GTM; culture described as a challenger mindset with speed, accountability and differentiated rewards.
- [Presented by] Deck was presented at the SCHIL Institutional Investor Meet on 24 March 2026 by Himanshu Bakshi, Managing Director.

themes.title: Consumption revival & FMCG premiumization
themes.need: Rural recovery, GST 2.0 and premiumization still frame the theme, but Q1FY27 rewarded portfolio SHAPE over volume. TATACONSUM's growth businesses hit INR 1,300cr (+47%) and are now 36% of India - larger than either salt (>INR 1,000cr) or tea & coffee (INR 1,200cr), with Sampann +58%, RTD +41% and Capital Foods INR 232cr (+40%) - while India tea revenue fell 4% on +2% volume as lower tea costs were deliberately passed back (tea inflation is now running 7-10% with most buying still ahead, so that inverts next year). PGHH shows the margin route: FY26 sales roughly flat at ~INR 4,300cr but PAT +19% to ~INR 850cr and ~100bps of structural margin from INR 86cr of productivity savings, absorbing crude and resin each up 30-50% with no stock-outs. The cautionary tale is licensed brands - JYOTHYLAB lost the Pril and Fa licences when Henkel did not renew (all manufacturing and selling stopped 1-June; Pril was ~7-8% of revenue, ~INR 225-240cr) and has filed SIAC arbitration. MARICO/DABUR/GODREJCP/COLPAL/EMAMILTD ride distribution + premium mix; VBL on beverage route-to-market; BIKAJI/GOPAL/BECTORFOOD on branded snacks; ORKLAINDIA took a 4% blended price increase in Q4 plus premium mix to a 16.9% EBITDA margin.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull-through; rural volume recovery; festive/wedding restocking; commodity pass-back timing; JYOTHYLAB's ~7-8% revenue hole and the SIAC arbitration.
